name: score-hold-2026-10-05
_note: SF-R HOLD arm (SCORE_FINISH_SPEC.md §4.2), written blind on October 5, 2026 by an agent that read only the turn-1 boot briefing and the help text. 20 questions (turn 1) and 20 orders (turn 2), each with its intended reading. Re-written fresh each scoring run; never edited after the run.

questions.line: where is mack?
questions.intended: Mack is at Swabia, but the reading is only partial, taken from a stale report.

questions.line: The dispatch says enemy strength is 44% of ours. Does that count the Russians, or only the armies we've actually spotted?
questions.intended: The 44% is only an estimate built from the 2 known corps read from stale reports, so unscouted armies such as any Russian force are not counted in it.

questions.line: how much gold have we got
questions.intended: The treasury holds 800g, with +1032 a turn expected by the accounts.

questions.line: Why am I paying extra upkeep? What is this force limit and how do I get it higher?
questions.intended: We field more men than the 130,000-man force limit, so the excess pays up to double upkeep (+1118g), and the limit grows with territory.

questions.line: who's in the Third Coalition besides Britain?
questions.intended: Names the coalition's members under Britain's lead (we are at war with Britain, Austria and Russia) and gives the threat at 70/100, Formed.

questions.line: Berthier, which of my marshals can get at Mack soonest?
questions.intended: Names the marshal who can reach Mack at Swabia first; the TODAY list shows Ney at Rhineland can attack him at once, with Davout beside him.

questions.line: What are Ney's chances if he attacks Mack right now?
questions.intended: Forecasts Ney's 24,000 against Mack at Swabia and warns that Mack's strength is only a partial estimate.

questions.line: How many turns would it take Davout to march from Rhineland to Lorraine?
questions.intended: States how many turns Davout's march from Rhineland to Lorraine would take.

questions.line: what does the Staff law actually do, and what would it cost me to enact it?
questions.intended: Explains that a reform law cures our doctrine's flaw only while the Staff stands, and quotes the Staff's terms: gold or authority once, gold every turn, and 1 Admin AP to enact.

questions.line: whats the flaw in our doctrine
questions.intended: Our doctrine is the Corps System; its flaw is living off the land beyond the frontier, which a reform law cures while the Staff stands.

questions.line: are we at war with Prussia? Brunswick is sitting in Berlin
questions.intended: Says whether France is at war with Prussia (the war purposes name only Britain, Austria and Russia) and that Brunswick at Berlin is only a partial reading.

questions.line: Who is Deroy and whose side is he on? He's in Franconia with Bernadotte.
questions.intended: Names Deroy's nation and whether he is friend or foe, noting he is read at full intelligence in Franconia, where Bernadotte also stands.

questions.line: where are the russians
questions.intended: No Russian army appears in our intelligence, so a good answer says they are unscouted rather than guessing where they stand.

questions.line: How many soldiers do we have in total?
questions.intended: Totals our army at 189,000 men across eight commanders, Massena's 42,000 the largest, well above the 130,000-man force limit.

questions.line: how much would it cost to recruit cavalry for Murat?
questions.intended: Quotes the gold price of a cavalry levy for Murat at Franche-Comte, which is x3 at war, dearer above the force limit and +15% for Murat's administration, plus 1 Admin AP.

questions.line: How many action points do I have to spend this turn?
questions.intended: States the action points available this turn (military, admin and diplomatic) and what the suggested orders would cost.

questions.line: Talleyrand, would Austria take a white peace right now?
questions.intended: Gives Austria's likely answer to a white peace, which the war purpose against Austria lists as the current settlement (+0) with all 28 of our provinces held.

questions.line: will bernadotte actualy obey me? the help says he may not march for me at all
questions.intended: Explains Bernadotte's 'Eyes on a Crown' and how far he can be trusted to march, pointing to his trust on his card on the Generals screen (G).

questions.line: What happens if I order Davout to fortify in the Rhineland?
questions.intended: Davout digs in for growing defense and his Iron Resolve coils +8% a turn, but he cannot move or attack while fortified.

questions.line: how many more provinces do we need before we can summon the Congress of Paris?
questions.intended: We hold 28 provinces against the 50 titled ones the Congress needs, so 22 more, with Paris held, the Emperor free and no satellite on the brink.

orders.line: Ney, if Mack's still in Swabia, attack him
I want Lannes to march to Swabia and attack Mack once he gets there
Have Murat ride out and scout the Tyrol
Tell Massena to fortfy at Milan in case Archduke John comes down from the Tyrol
Davout, leave a garrison behind in the Rhineland
Have Davout head over to Lorraine and dig in there
Could Soult drill his corps today?
Bernadotte, stay put in Franconia and hold it
Napoleon, take up a defensive position in Lorraine
If Ney beat Mack, give him a rente for it
Buy substitutes to fill out Ney's ranks
raise more infantry for Davout's corps
recruit some calvary for Murat
If we can still afford it, put a supply depot up in the Rhineland
Please pass the Staff law
Talleyrand, go and improve our relations with Prussia
Propose a white peace to Austria
lay down a couple of new ships
Have the fleet guard our home waters
Commission another marshal
